title: Digital Renaissance Editions
institution: University of Victoria (Internet Shakespeare Editions platform), with the University of Leeds and the University of Western Australia
notes: Scholarly editions of early English plays and interludes, each with a diplomatic (old-spelling) transcription of the early printed or manuscript witness next to a modern-spelling text. Three peer-reviewed editions are complete (The Honest Whore, Parts 1 and 2, and An Humorous Day's Mirth); the Annex adds about 18 further proofread, unreviewed old-spelling play texts (for example Cambyses, Arden of Faversham, Fair Em, Mankind-era interludes). Everything is readable online without login. No text or word count is given: the site publishes none, and the plays are not individually dated in a list that could be counted reliably. The content pages record 'Last Modified' dates of 2014-2015 and the Annex text folders on the server date from 2021-07-14, with nothing newer found, so it is marked archived. Copyright policy: free for educational, non-profit use. The same site is also listed under its http:// address.
